operations.detail: Automatic-compensation rules are bound to the official page revision dated 20 July 2026.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Automatic compensation is a voluntary code applying through participating providers, not a universal coverage dataset.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Eligible compensation is designed to be paid without the customer separately requesting the payment.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Payment amounts increase annually in line with inflation.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Annual increases use CPI as of 31 October in the previous year.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Updated amounts apply from 1 April to new service issues.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: A provider not listed as a signatory is not assumed to owe payments under the voluntary scheme.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The scheme covers residential fixed broadband and landline products.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The consumer compensation scheme is not treated as business-premise coverage evidence.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The fixed broadband and landline scheme is not substituted for mobile coverage evidence.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Delayed-repair compensation concerns a service that has stopped working.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Delayed-repair entitlement starts when the service is not fully fixed after two full working days.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: For loss of service, the customer must report the fault to the provider.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The current initial delayed-repair payment is £10.34 after the two-full-working-day threshold.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The current delayed-repair amount is £10.34 for each qualifying full day.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Delayed-repair compensation is expressed per calendar day after the threshold.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: A scheduled engineer no-show is a compensable missed appointment.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Cancellation with less than 24 hours' notice is treated as a missed appointment.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The current missed-appointment amount is £32.31 per appointment.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Delayed-start compensation uses the provider's promised service-start date.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Failure to start the new service on the promised date is compensable.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The current delayed-start amount is £6.46 for each calendar day.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The missed start date is included in delayed-start compensation.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Unless an exclusion applies, events beyond customer or provider control do not automatically remove entitlement.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Extreme weather is given as an example of an event that can still be covered.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Strikes are given as an example of an event that can still be covered.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Third-party acts are given as an example of an event that can still be covered.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Simultaneous landline and broadband loss produces one compensation payment, not two.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: A compensation trigger records a service failure event, not whether a premise can order broadband.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Compensation values are never interpreted as broadband speed or coverage metrics.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Compensation is normally supplied as a bill credit unless otherwise agreed.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The credit should be applied no later than 30 calendar days after the qualifying resolution event.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: For loss of service, the payment clock follows repair or service termination.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: For a missed appointment, the payment clock follows the appointment date.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: For delayed start, the payment clock follows service activation or cancellation.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The account credit may be applied before it appears on a later bill.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Alternative compensation is allowed only at the same or higher value.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The provider should disclose the bill-credit value before offering another form.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: A missed service-start date should generate compensation without customer action.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: A missed appointment should generate compensation without customer action.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: After reporting a fault, the customer should not need a second compensation request.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Loss caused by equipment or activity within the home can be excluded.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Customer breach of contract can exclude payment.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: A failure caused by the customer can be excluded.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Preventing resolution can exclude payment.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Choosing a later engineer appointment and delaying repair is an exclusion example.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: A provider relying on an exception is expected to explain its reasons clearly.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Providers are expected to continue acting in the customer's best interests.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Where legitimate non-payment applies, customers should not be charged for service they are not receiving.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: After 30 days of compensation, a provider may issue a cease notification.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: A cease notification can state payments will stop after a further 30 days.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: After a cease notice, the provider must take reasonable steps to supply a suitable alternative.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Compensation continues when no suitable alternative service can be provided.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: A compensation-payment limit is not interpreted as a network availability limit.
operations.source: Ofcom automatic compensation guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: ADR rules are bound to the official page revision dated 20 July 2026.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The customer first contacts the provider's customer-services department.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: An unresolved problem should be escalated through the provider's formal complaint process.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Eligible customers have a right to use ADR free of charge.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: ADR schemes independently and impartially assess complaints.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Residential customers are eligible for the described ADR route.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Small businesses with up to 10 employees are eligible.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Not-for-profit organisations with up to 10 workers, excluding volunteers, are eligible.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The complaint must already have been raised with the provider.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: ADR is available after six weeks or earlier with a deadlock letter.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The customer can request a deadlock letter when agreement cannot be reached.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Referral must be within 12 months of receiving a deadlock letter.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Phone and broadband providers must maintain an accessible complaints code of practice.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The complaints code must include a phone contact.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The complaint phone number must be free or charged at geographic rate.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The complaints code must include a postal address.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The complaints code must include an email address or webform.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The code must describe investigation steps.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The code must describe complaint-resolution timeframes.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: The code must explain what to do if the customer remains unhappy.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Providers must take prompt and active steps to resolve complaints.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Providers must promptly communicate the outcome.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Ofcom currently approves CISAS and Communications Ombudsman.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: Provider membership determines which approved ADR scheme handles a complaint.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: ADR eligibility and membership are not evidence of network coverage.
operations.source: Ofcom ADR guide, updated 20 July 2026

operations.detail: General Condition C4 governs complaints handling and dispute resolution for relevant customers.

operations.detail: Providers must follow the Ofcom Approved Complaints Code.
operations.source: Ofcom codes of practice page, updated 16 July 2025

operations.detail: Providers must belong to and comply with an approved ADR scheme.
operations.source: Ofcom codes of practice page, updated 16 July 2025

operations.detail: Failure to comply with formal requirements can lead to enforcement penalties.
operations.source: Ofcom codes of practice page, updated 16 July 2025

operations.detail: Updated broadband speed codes apply to purchases from 21 December 2022.
operations.source: Ofcom codes of practice page, updated 16 July 2025

operations.detail: Residential speed-code signatories are maintained separately from business signatories.
operations.source: Ofcom codes of practice page, updated 16 July 2025

operations.detail: Business speed-code signatories are maintained separately from residential signatories.
operations.source: Ofcom codes of practice page, updated 16 July 2025

operations.detail: Telephone extension leads and wiring changes can introduce interference and reduce speed.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: Where an extension is necessary, a short high-quality cable is advised.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: Tangled or coiled cables can affect broadband speed.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: Microfilters should be used on each phone socket in use where applicable.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: A problem affecting one device more than others is treated as a device-level diagnostic clue.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: Current security software is advised when diagnosing device-specific problems.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: A network-service fault should be diagnosed and handled by the provider.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: For a network fault, the provider should explain how and when it will be fixed.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: Priority fault repair is offered for eligible customers with disability-related urgent need.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: Prolonged loss can, depending on contract terms and obligations, support leaving without penalty.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: Speeds far below the original estimate may engage voluntary speed-code protections.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: A missed promised repair date supports use of the formal complaints process.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: An unresolved fault complaint can be referred to ADR after six weeks.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: A deadlock letter can enable ADR referral before six weeks.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: Ofcom does not itself investigate individual complaints through this guide.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: Complaint information can support Ofcom monitoring of systemic problems.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: In-home fault diagnostics are not substituted for premise-level availability evidence.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: Consumer troubleshooting guidance is not a measured-speed dataset.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026

operations.detail: Compensation, ADR, codes and fault guides remain one Ofcom source family for source counting.
operations.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide, updated 8 April 2026
